# PRB-005: Databases are not reachable from the internet

- **Group:** Outside view
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

PostgreSQL (5432), MySQL and MariaDB (3306), Redis (6379), MongoDB (27017) and Elasticsearch (9200) on a public port are found by scanners within hours and attacked with default or guessed credentials; Redis and Elasticsearch often answer without any. A platform's "publicly available" database toggle is the usual cause. The host side of this is PAAS-004 and the Docker published port checks.

## Verify by hand

```sh
for p in 5432 3306 6379 27017 9200; do nc -vz -w 3 <host> $p; done   # from another machine
```

## How to fix it

Turn off public publishing of the database (or publish it on 127.0.0.1), and reach it over the tailnet or an SSH tunnel.

## What a fix can break

Clients that connect to the database over the internet stop working; move them to the tailnet first.

Run `stackward explain PRB-005` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
